mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: stronger particle vibrations -> particles leave fixed positions -> solid changes happens first, and that produces added heat.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Melting point is defined at atmospheric pressure is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: When a solid is heated, its particles vibrate more vigorously until they can start leaving their positions; the minimum temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid at atmospheric pressure is its melting point. added heat -> stronger particle vibrations -> particles leave fixed positions -> solid changes to liquid at its melting point The learner connects added heat to stronger particle vibrations, particles leaving fixed positions, and the solid becoming liquid at its melting point under atmospheric pressure. Melting point is just a number in a table; heat changes state without a particle-motion reason.
